classification.difficultyReason: Count multiples within a bounded three-digit interval, connect simultaneous divisibility to common multiples, and reconstruct disjoint three-set regions before evaluating compound events.

content.prompt: A three-digit number is chosen at random.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Describe the sample space and draw a Venn diagram with sets for numbers divisible by 3, 5 and 7.

answer.short:
$\xi=\{100,101,\ldots,999\}$ and $|\xi|=900$.

The diagram shows the number of outcomes in each region.
answer.worked:
There are $999-100+1=900$ equally likely outcomes. Let $T$, $F$ and $S$ contain the numbers divisible by 3, 5 and 7 respectively.

Count multiples from the first to the last in the sample space:
$$\begin{align*}|T|&=333-34+1=300\\|F|&=199-20+1=180\\|S|&=142-15+1=128\\|T\cap F|&=66-7+1=60\\|T\cap S|&=47-5+1=43\\|F\cap S|&=28-3+1=26\\|T\cap F\cap S|&=9-1+1=9\end{align*}$$
Fill the triple intersection first, then the pair-only regions:
$$\begin{align*}|T\cap F\cap S'|&=60-9=51\\|T\cap S\cap F'|&=43-9=34\\|F\cap S\cap T'|&=26-9=17\end{align*}$$
The single-set regions are:
$$\begin{align*}|T\cap F'\cap S'|&=300-51-34-9=206\\|F\cap T'\cap S'|&=180-51-17-9=103\\|S\cap T'\cap F'|&=128-34-17-9=68\end{align*}$$
The union contains $206+103+68+51+34+17+9=488$ outcomes, leaving $900-488=412$ outside all three sets.

children.prompt: Find the probability that the number is divisible by:

answer.worked:
The common multiples are multiples of 35. The diagram gives $17+9=26$ outcomes.
$$\begin{align*}P(F\cap S)&=\frac{26}{900}\\P(F\cap S)&=\frac{13}{450}\end{align*}$$

Count the overlap once.
$$\begin{align*}|F\cup S|&=180+128-26\\|F\cup S|&=282\\P(F\cup S)&=\frac{282}{900}\\P(F\cup S)&=\frac{47}{150}\end{align*}$$

The common multiples are multiples of 105. There are 9 in the triple intersection.
$$\begin{align*}P(T\cap F\cap S)&=\frac9{900}\\P(T\cap F\cap S)&=\frac1{100}\end{align*}$$

Exclude the triple intersection from the 60 multiples of 15.
$$\begin{align*}|T\cap F\cap S'|&=60-9=51\\P(T\cap F\cap S')&=\frac{51}{900}\\P(T\cap F\cap S')&=\frac{17}{300}\end{align*}$$

Exclude the triple intersection from the 26 multiples of 35.
$$\begin{align*}|F\cap S\cap T'|&=26-9=17\\P(F\cap S\cap T')&=\frac{17}{900}\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$\frac{122}{225}$

Count every region inside the three circles once.
answer.worked:
There are 412 outcomes outside all three sets.
$$\begin{align*}|T\cup F\cup S|&=900-412\\|T\cup F\cup S|&=488\\P(T\cup F\cup S)&=\frac{488}{900}\\P(T\cup F\cup S)&=\frac{122}{225}\end{align*}$$
